contents.name: §1 The Classical KAM-Theorem, statement of the theorem for H=h+f: real analytic nondegenerate perturbation, Diophantine frequencies, persistence for ε≪α²
contents.support: The local theorem assembles the same statement from the local chain: explicit analytic data, the ε≤cα² threshold via the reduction lemma, and the positive-measure conclusion via the slab estimate.

contents.name: §1, measure of the Diophantine set: |k·ω|≥α|k|_1^{-τ} with τ>n-1 and mes(D_α∩B)=mes(B)-O(α)
contents.support: The slab estimate and the complement/measure clauses reproduce this with an explicit constant C_{n,τ} and the τ>n-1 convergence condition.

contents.name: §2 The KAM Theorem with Parameters, the domains D_{r,s}, the parameter neighbourhood O_h and the sup-norm
contents.support: The definition fixes the angular torus, the action-angle neighbourhoods D_{r,s,h}(Ω), holomorphy, sup-norms, Fourier data and the label set Ω_{α,τ} with the same conventions.

contents.name: §2, analytic estimates: Cauchy bounds, Fourier decay, lattice shell counting and the exponential small-divisor sums
contents.support: Clauses 1-4 reproduce the Fourier decay |g_k|≤M e^{-(s-σ)|k|_1}, the Cauchy bounds, the shell count 4^n m^{n-1} and the truncation estimate.

contents.name: §2-§3, the parametrized theorem and the linearized equation ⟨ω,∂_θu⟩=v solved by Fourier series with uniform small divisors on O_h
contents.support: The lemma solves the homological equation coefficientwise, with the conservative loss μ=τ+3n+2 and the uniform bound on the complex parameter ball h≤α/(2K^{τ+1}).

contents.name: §3 Outline of the Proof of Theorem A: the affine splitting Q=P(0,θ)+P_I(0,θ)I, the Taylor estimate and the Fourier truncation R=T_KQ
contents.support: The truncation lemma proves exactly these estimates, including the quadratic Taylor remainder and the exponential tail bound.

contents.name: §3-§4, the generator F with {F,N}+R̂=R, its estimates, the time-one flow of X_F and the transformed perturbation
contents.support: The generator-flow lemma constructs F, estimates its weighted derivatives, integrates its flow with explicit domain control and derives ε_+≤C[E+η²+σ^{-n}e^{-σK/2}]ε.

contents.name: §3, the parameter retraction ν=ν₊+v(ν) by a contraction with |Dv|≤2nB/h≤1/8
contents.support: The contraction lemma solves ν+v(ν)=ν₊ on a complex ball and proves the derivative bounds h‖Dφ-I‖≤(16n/7)B.

contents.name: §4-§5, the geometric sequences σ_j,K_j,h_j,s_j and the simultaneous choice of K_0, E_0, h_0
contents.support: The sequences lemma verifies every step hypothesis at every stage with explicit conditions on K_0σ_0, E_0 and h_0.

contents.name: §5 Iteration and Proof of Theorem A: weighted composed Jacobians, convergence of the corrections on I=0 and passage to the limit
contents.support: The composed-map lemma proves uniform convergence with all angular derivatives, the size bounds and the frequency-Lipschitz bound.

contents.name: §5, invariance and Lagrangian character of the limiting torus: X_H∘Φ=DΦ·X_N
contents.support: The limit theorem proves the invariance identity, the quasi-periodic motion and the vanishing pullback from the finite-step normal forms.

contents.name: §5, the limiting torus as an embedded torus and its closeness to the unperturbed one
contents.support: The embedding lemma proves injectivity modulo 2π, rank n of the differential, the descent to the torus and the Lipschitz inverse.

contents.name: §5, elimination of the parameters via p=b(ω)+I and the reduction of the smallness to ε≤cα²
contents.support: The reduction lemma proves the Taylor decomposition with |P_h|≤M_2|I|², the choice r=√(ε/M_2) and the equivalence of 2ε≤c_1αrσ_0^μ with ε≤(c_1²/4)α²σ_0^{2μ}/M_2.

contents.name: Appendix A: Some Facts about Analytic Functions (Cauchy estimates on polydiscs, the implicit function theorem in analytic form)
contents.support: The Cauchy and majorant estimates are absorbed into the local Fourier/Cauchy lemma; the analytic implicit-function part is supplied by the published root item thm-real-analytic-inverse-and-implicit-function-theorems and is recorded as absorbed, not rebuilt.

contents.name: Appendix B: Lipschitz Functions (extension of the frequency parametrisation)
contents.reason: The Whitney-type extension device of Appendix B is not a load-bearing premise here: all estimates are made directly on the closed label set Ω_{α,τ} with Cauchy bounds and uniqueness of the retraction, so no Lipschitz extension of the frequency map is built.

contents.name: §3, the sharper small-divisor loss stated on p. 18
contents.reason: The sharper exponent is stated in the source without a complete local proof carrying it; the local development consistently uses only the proved conservative exponent μ=τ+3n+2, and the constants adapt without changing any claim.

sources.title: Rafael de la Llave, A Tutorial on KAM Theory (expanded version of the Seattle 1999 lectures, AMS Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 69; complete 135-page PDF)
sources.locator: §3.1 pp. 24-31, §3.3 pp. 32-36, §3.4 pp. 36-40, §3.5 pp. 40-49, §3.6 pp. 49-58, §6.1 pp. 92-100, §6.2 pp. 100-106, §6.3 pp. 106-110, §6.4 pp. 110-118 (printed/PDF pages coincide); table of contents and sections inspected in the complete PDF fetched for this batch

contents.name: §3.1 Preliminaries in analysis: analytic norms, Fourier coefficients and complexification of real analytic data
contents.support: Supplies the second treatment of the analytic framework fixed in the definition (domains, norms, periodic data, complexification).

contents.name: §3.1, analytic norms and Fourier coefficient estimates
contents.support: The same Cauchy/Fourier estimates are absorbed into the local lemma, which is proved from first principles with the lattice-shell count.

contents.name: §3.3 Diophantine properties: Diophantine numbers of type (K,ν), the higher-dimensional conditions and the measure of the resonant sets
contents.support: Independent treatment of the small-divisor slabs and of the positive measure of the Diophantine complement; the local lemma reproves the estimate with explicit constants.

contents.name: §3.4 Estimates for the linearized equation: small-divisor estimates for the cohomological equation ω·∂_θh=g
contents.support: Second treatment of the coefficientwise solution of the homological equation and of the divergence of the small divisors as σ→0.

contents.name: §3.5 Geometric structures: symplectic forms, Lagrangian submanifolds and canonical maps
contents.support: The Lagrangian comparison criteria are absorbed into the pullback computation of the limit theorem; no separate geometric item is built.

contents.name: §3.6 Canonical perturbation theory: generating functions and the quadratic remainder of a Newton step
contents.support: The perturbation-theory step is absorbed into the generator/flow lemma, which constructs the correcting map and estimates its remainder.

contents.name: §4 Two KAM proofs in a model problem
contents.reason: The model problem is used in the source only to exhibit the two iteration schemes on a simple map; the local development follows the parametrized Kolmogorov scheme of Pöschel, so the model computation is not rebuilt here.

contents.name: §5 Hard implicit function theorems
contents.reason: The abstract Nash-Moser machinery is not used: the local scheme is the concrete quadratic iteration with explicit sequences verifying every step hypothesis, so no hard implicit function theorem is built.

contents.name: §6 Persistence of invariant tori for quasi-integrable systems
contents.support: Second treatment of the persistence statement, its hypotheses and the positive-measure conclusion; used as the independent comparison for the assembled theorem.

contents.name: §6.1 Kolmogorov's method: composed Newton transformations and uniformity in the parameter
contents.support: The convergence of the composed transformations and the uniformity of the estimates are the content of the local composed-map lemma.

contents.name: §6.2 Arnol'd method: geometric-sequences bookkeeping for the quadratic iteration
contents.support: The geometric-sequences bookkeeping is absorbed into the sequences lemma, which verifies all step hypotheses at every stage.

contents.name: §6.3 Lagrangian proof: the invariant torus as a Lagrangian submanifold
contents.support: The Lagrangian character is absorbed into the embedding lemma and the limit theorem; no separate Lagrangian-formalism development is built.

contents.name: §6.4 Proof without changes of variables
contents.reason: This is an alternative proof of the same theorem; the local development follows the parametrized scheme, and building a second proof route is not among the promises of this pair.

contents.name: §1 Introduction and §1.1 Some recent developments
contents.reason: Literature survey of later developments; it states no result that the CM KAM pair promises to build, and no estimate or construction is taken from it.

contents.name: §2.2 Siegel disks
contents.reason: The Siegel-disk example belongs to holomorphic dynamics, outside the non-relativistic classical-mechanics mathematics scope of this pair.

contents.name: §7 Some remarks on computer assisted proofs
contents.reason: Computer-assisted validation is outside the mathematical scope of this pair and no numerical certification is claimed anywhere in the batch.

contents.name: §1, the general perturbation form H=h(p)+f_ε(p,q) with real analytic data and the ε≪α² smallness
contents.support: The example specialises the general form to h(I)=½|I|² and F=εcosθ₁cosθ₂ and checks the theorem's data with explicit constants.

contents.name: §1-§2, the measure of the Diophantine set in a bounded frequency region
contents.support: The example evaluates the slab bound for n=2, τ=2 and the frequency square (1.2,1.8)² and obtains the explicit positivity threshold α<4.7×10^{-3}.
